passages.text: Then Josiah celebrated the Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king in Jerusalem.
Josiah celebrated the Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem.
The people slaughtered the Passover lamb.
They did this on the fourteenth day of the first month.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יֹאשִׁיָּ֧הוּ בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם פֶּ֖סַח לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁחֲט֣וּ הַפֶּ֔סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: He appointed the priests to their duties and encouraged them in the service of the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah gave the priests their duties.
He made sure the priests stood at their posts.
He encouraged the priests.
He strengthened them to serve in the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲמֵ֥ד הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים עַל־ מִשְׁמְרוֹתָ֑ם וַֽיְחַזְּקֵ֔ם לַעֲבוֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: To the Levites who taught all Israel and were holy to the LORD, Josiah said: “Put the holy ark in the temple built by Solomon son of David king of Israel. It is not to be carried around on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah spoke to the Levites.
The Levites taught all Israel.
The Levites were holy to the LORD.
Josiah said to the Levites, “Put the holy ark in the temple.
Solomon, son of David, king of Israel, built this temple.
Do not carry the ark on your shoulders anymore.
Now serve the LORD your God.
Also serve His people Israel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לַ֠לְוִיִּם הַמְּבוּנִים לְכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הַקְּדוֹשִׁ֣ים לַיהוָ֗ה תְּנ֤וּ אֶת־ אֲרוֹן־ הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ בַּ֠בַּיִת אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֜ה שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בֶן־ דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵין־ לָכֶ֥ם מַשָּׂ֖א בַּכָּתֵ֑ף עַתָּ֗ה עִבְדוּ֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת עַמּ֥וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Prepare yourselves by families in your divisions, according to the instructions written by David king of Israel and Solomon his son.
passages.sermon:
David was king of Israel.
Solomon was David’s son.
David and Solomon gave written instructions.
You belong to families and divisions.
Prepare yourselves by your family groups.
Follow the instructions from David and Solomon.
passages.original: וְהָכִ֥ונוּ לְבֵית־ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם כְּמַחְלְקוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם בִּכְתָ֗ב דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבְמִכְתַּ֖ב שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Moreover, stand in the Holy Place by the divisions of the families of your kinsmen the lay people, and by the divisions of the families of the Levites.
passages.sermon:
The Levites served God in the temple.
The Levites were holy to the LORD.
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah gave instructions to the Levites.
Josiah told the Levites to stand in the Holy Place.
The Levites must stand by the family groups of their fellow Israelites.
The Levites must also stand by the family groups of the Levites.
Each group must stand in its proper place.
Each group must stand according to its family division.
passages.original: וְעִמְד֣וּ בַקֹּ֗דֶשׁ לִפְלֻגּוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הָֽאָב֔וֹת לַאֲחֵיכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַחֲלֻקַּ֥ת בֵּֽית־ אָ֖ב לַלְוִיִּֽם׃

passages.text: Slaughter the Passover lambs, consecrate yourselves, and make preparations for your fellow countrymen to carry out the word of the LORD given by Moses.”
passages.sermon:
The Levites must act.
They must slaughter the Passover lambs.
They must consecrate themselves.
They must prepare for their fellow Israelites.
They must do everything as the LORD commanded through Moses.
passages.original: וְשַׁחֲט֖וּ הַפָּ֑סַח וְהִתְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ וְהָכִ֣ינוּ לַאֲחֵיכֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כִּדְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

passages.text: From his own flocks and herds Josiah contributed 30,000 lambs and goats plus 3,000 bulls for the Passover offerings for all the people who were present.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was the king of Judah.
Josiah gave animals for the Passover offerings.
He gave from his own flocks and herds.
He gave 30,000 lambs and goats.
He also gave 3,000 bulls.
He gave these animals for all the people who were present.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣רֶם יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ לִבְנֵ֪י הָעָ֟ם צֹ֞אן כְּבָשִׂ֣ים וּבְנֵֽי־ עִזִּים֮ הַכֹּ֣ל לַפְּסָחִים֒ לְכָל־ הַנִּמְצָ֗א לְמִסְפַּר֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וּבָקָ֖ר שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֑ים אֵ֖לֶּה מֵרְכ֥וּשׁ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: His officials also contributed willingly to the people and priests and Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the administrators of the house of God, gave the priests 2,600 Passover offerings and 300 bulls.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah had officials.
These officials gave gifts willingly.
They gave gifts to the people.
They gave gifts to the priests.
They gave gifts to the Levites.
Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel were administrators of the house of God.
Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel gave gifts to the priests.
They gave 2,600 Passover offerings to the priests.
They gave 300 bulls to the priests.
passages.original: וְשָׂרָ֞יו לִנְדָבָ֥ה לָעָ֛ם לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֖ם הֵרִ֑ימוּ חִלְקִיָּ֨ה וּזְכַרְיָ֜הוּ וִֽיחִיאֵ֗ל נְגִידֵי֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לַכֹּהֲנִ֞ים נָתְנ֣וּ לַפְּסָחִ֗ים אַלְפַּ֙יִם֙ וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת וּבָקָ֖ר שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Additionally, Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, as well as Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, officers of the Levites, donated to the Levites 5,000 Passover offerings and 500 bulls.
passages.sermon:
Conaniah was an officer of the Levites.
Shemaiah and Nethanel were his brothers.
Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad were also officers of the Levites.
These six men gave gifts to the Levites.
They gave 5,000 animals for the Passover sacrifice.
They also gave 500 bulls.
passages.original: וְכָונַנְיָהוּ וּשְׁמַֽעְיָ֨הוּ וּנְתַנְאֵ֜ל אֶחָ֗יו וַחֲשַׁבְיָ֧הוּ וִיעִיאֵ֛ל וְיוֹזָבָ֖ד שָׂרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֑ם הֵרִ֨ימוּ לַלְוִיִּ֤ם לַפְּסָחִים֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים וּבָקָ֖ר חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: So the service was prepared; the priests stood in their places and the Levites in their divisions according to the king’s command.
passages.sermon:
The priests and Levites served in the temple.
The priests and Levites followed the king’s command.
The priests stood in their assigned places.
The Levites stood in their assigned divisions.
The service was ready.
passages.original: וַתִּכּ֖וֹן הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה וַיַּֽעַמְד֨וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים עַל־ עָמְדָ֛ם וְהַלְוִיִּ֥ם עַל־ מַחְלְקוֹתָ֖ם כְּמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And they slaughtered the Passover lambs, while the priests sprinkled the blood handed to them and the Levites skinned the animals.
passages.sermon:
The Levites and priests served in the temple.
The people brought Passover lambs for sacrifice.
They slaughtered the Passover lambs.
The priests took the blood from the lambs.
The priests sprinkled the blood as required.
The Levites skinned the animals.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ הַפָּ֑סַח וַיִּזְרְק֤וּ הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם וְהַלְוִיִּ֖ם מַפְשִׁיטִֽים׃

passages.text: They set aside the burnt offerings to be given to the divisions of the families of the people to offer to the LORD, as is written in the Book of Moses; and they did the same with the bulls.
passages.sermon:
The priests and Levites prepared the burnt offerings.
They set aside these offerings for the family groups of the people.
Each family group received its portion.
The people offered these portions to the LORD.
This followed what is written in the Book of Moses.
They also set aside the bulls in the same way.
passages.original: וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ הָעֹלָ֜ה לְ֠תִתָּם לְמִפְלַגּ֤וֹת לְבֵית־ אָבוֹת֙ לִבְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם לְהַקְרִיב֙ לַיהוָ֔ה כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּסֵ֣פֶר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְכֵ֖ן לַבָּקָֽר׃

passages.text: They roasted the Passover animals on the fire according to the regulation, and they boiled the other holy offerings in pots, kettles, and bowls and quickly brought them to all the people.
passages.sermon:
The Levites and priests prepared the Passover animals for the people of Israel.
They roasted the Passover animals over the fire.
They followed the regulation for roasting the Passover animals.
They boiled the other holy offerings.
They used pots, kettles, and bowls to boil the holy offerings.
They quickly brought the food to all the people.
passages.original: וַֽיְבַשְּׁל֥וּ הַפֶּ֛סַח בָּאֵ֖שׁ כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְהַקֳּדָשִׁ֣ים בִּשְּׁל֗וּ בַּסִּיר֤וֹת וּבַדְּוָדִים֙ וּבַצֵּ֣לָח֔וֹת וַיָּרִ֖יצוּ לְכָל־ בְּנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Afterward, they made preparations for themselves and for the priests, since the priests, the descendants of Aaron, were offering up burnt offerings and fat until nightfall. So the Levites made preparations for themselves and for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
passages.sermon:
The priests were descendants of Aaron.
The priests offered burnt offerings and fat until nightfall.
The Levites made preparations for themselves.
The Levites also made preparations for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
passages.original: וְאַחַ֗ר הֵכִ֤ינוּ לָהֶם֙ וְלַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים כִּ֤י הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן בְּהַֽעֲל֛וֹת הָעוֹלָ֥ה וְהַחֲלָבִ֖ים עַד־ לָ֑יְלָה וְהַלְוִיִּם֙ הֵכִ֣ינוּ לָהֶ֔ם וְלַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹֽן׃

passages.text: The singers, the descendants of Asaph, were at their stations according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king’s seer. And the gatekeepers at each gate did not need to leave their position, because their fellow Levites made preparations for them.
passages.sermon:
The singers were descendants of Asaph.
They stood at their stations.
They followed the command of David.
They also followed the command of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun.
Jeduthun was the king’s seer.
The gatekeepers stood at each gate.
The gatekeepers did not need to leave their position.
Their fellow Levites made preparations for them.
passages.original: וְהַמְשֹֽׁרֲרִ֨ים בְּנֵי־ אָסָ֜ף עַל־ מַעֲמָדָ֗ם כְּמִצְוַ֤ת דָּוִיד֙ וְאָסָ֞ף וְהֵימָ֤ן וִֽידֻתוּן֙ חוֹזֵ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְהַשֹּׁעֲרִ֖ים לְשַׁ֣עַר וָשָׁ֑עַר אֵ֣ין לָהֶ֗ם לָסוּר֙ מֵעַ֣ל עֲבֹֽדָתָ֔ם כִּֽי־ אֲחֵיהֶ֥ם הַלְוִיִּ֖ם הֵכִ֥ינוּ לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So on that day the entire service of the LORD was carried out for celebrating the Passover and offering burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
passages.sermon:
King Josiah gave a command.
The people obeyed his command.
They carried out the entire service of the LORD on that day.
They celebrated the Passover.
They offered burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD.
They did all these things as King Josiah commanded.
passages.original: וַ֠תִּכּוֹן כָּל־ עֲבוֹדַ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔סַח וְהַעֲל֣וֹת עֹל֔וֹת עַ֖ל מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֑ה כְּמִצְוַ֖ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: The Israelites who were present also observed the Passover at that time, as well as the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were present at that time.
They observed the Passover.
They also observed the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
They kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֛ים אֶת־ הַפֶּ֖סַח בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וְאֶת־ חַ֥ג הַמַּצּ֖וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: No such Passover had been observed in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet. None of the kings of Israel ever observed a Passover like the one that Josiah observed with the priests, the Levites, all Judah, the Israelites who were present, and the people of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah observed the Passover.
The priests and the Levites joined Josiah.
All Judah joined Josiah.
The Israelites who were present joined Josiah.
The people of Jerusalem joined Josiah.
No Passover like this had been observed in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet.
None of the kings of Israel had ever observed a Passover like this one.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ נַעֲשָׂ֨ה פֶ֤סַח כָּמֹ֙הוּ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִימֵ֖י שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל הַנָּבִ֑יא וְכָל־ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל׀ לֹֽא־ עָשׂ֡וּ כַּפֶּ֣סַח אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֣ה יֹֽ֠אשִׁיָּהוּ וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֤ם וְכָל־ יְהוּדָה֙ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הַנִּמְצָ֔א וְיוֹשְׁבֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: In the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign, this Passover was observed.
passages.sermon: Josiah was king of Judah.\r\nHe ruled for eighteen years.\r\nIn the eighteenth year of his reign, the people observed the Passover.
passages.original: בִּשְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְמַלְכ֖וּת יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ נַעֲשָׂ֖ה הַפֶּ֥סַח הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: After all this, when Josiah had set the temple in order, Neco king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to confront him.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah set the temple in order.
After Josiah finished this work, something happened.
Neco was king of Egypt.
Neco marched up to fight at Carchemish.
Carchemish was by the Euphrates River.
Josiah went out to confront Neco.
passages.original: אַחֲרֵ֣י כָל־ זֹ֗את אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵכִ֤ין יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶת־ הַבַּ֔יִת עָלָ֞ה נְכ֧וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֛יִם לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם בְּכַרְכְּמִ֖ישׁ עַל־ פְּרָ֑ת וַיֵּצֵ֥א לִקְרָאת֖וֹ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: But Neco sent messengers to him, saying, “What is the issue between you and me, O king of Judah? I have not come against you today, but I am fighting another dynasty. God told me to hurry; so stop opposing God, who is with me, or He will destroy you!”
passages.sermon:
Neco was the king of Egypt.
Neco sent messengers to Josiah.
The messengers spoke for Neco.
They said, “King of Judah, what is the issue between you and me?”
They said, “I have not come against you today.”
They said, “I am fighting another dynasty.”
They said, “God told me to hurry.”
They said, “Stop opposing God, who is with me.”
They said, “If you do not stop, God will destroy you.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אֵלָ֣יו מַלְאָכִ֣ים׀ לֵאמֹר֩׀ מַה־ לִּ֨י וָלָ֜ךְ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה לֹא־ עָלֶ֨יךָ אַתָּ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ כִּ֚י אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית מִלְחַמְתִּ֔י וֵאלֹהִ֖ים אָמַ֣ר לְבַֽהֲלֵ֑נִי חֲדַל־ לְךָ֛ מֵאֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ עִמִּ֖י וְאַל־ יַשְׁחִיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Josiah, however, did not turn away from him; instead, in order to engage him in battle, he disguised himself. He did not listen to Neco’s words from the mouth of God, but went to fight him on the Plain of Megiddo.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah did not turn away from Neco, king of Egypt.
Josiah wanted to fight Neco.
Josiah disguised himself to go into battle.
Josiah did not listen to Neco’s words.
Neco’s words came from God.
Josiah went to fight Neco on the Plain of Megiddo.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ הֵסֵב֩ יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ פָנָ֜יו מִמֶּ֗נּוּ כִּ֤י לְהִלָּחֵֽם־ בּוֹ֙ הִתְחַפֵּ֔שׂ וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע אֶל־ דִּבְרֵ֥י נְכ֖וֹ מִפִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֕א לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בְּבִקְעַ֥ת מְגִדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: There the archers shot King Josiah, who said to his servants, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded!”
passages.sermon:
King Josiah was in battle at Megiddo.
Archers shot King Josiah.
King Josiah was badly wounded.
King Josiah spoke to his servants.
He said, “Take me away.”
He said, “I am badly wounded.”
passages.original: וַיֹּרוּ֙ הַיֹּרִ֔ים לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ לַעֲבָדָיו֙ הַעֲבִיר֔וּנִי כִּ֥י הָחֳלֵ֖יתִי מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: So his servants took him out of his chariot, put him in his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem, where he died. And Josiah was buried in the tomb of his fathers, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for him.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was the king of Judah.
His servants took Josiah out of his chariot.
They put Josiah in his second chariot.
They brought Josiah to Jerusalem.
Josiah died in Jerusalem.
They buried Josiah in the tomb of his fathers.
All the people of Judah mourned for Josiah.
All the people of Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲבִירֻ֨הוּ עֲבָדָ֜יו מִן־ הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֗ה וַֽיַּרְכִּיבֻהוּ֮ עַ֣ל רֶ֣כֶב הַמִּשְׁנֶה֮ אֲשֶׁר־ לוֹ֒ וַיּוֹלִיכֻ֙הוּ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיָּ֕מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּקִבְר֣וֹת אֲבֹתָ֑יו וְכָל־ יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִֽתְאַבְּלִ֖ים עַל־ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ׃פ

passages.text: Then Jeremiah lamented over Josiah, and to this day all the choirs of men and women sing laments over Josiah. They established them as a statute for Israel, and indeed they are written in the Book of Laments.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet in Israel.
Josiah was the king of Judah.
Jeremiah lamented over Josiah.
Men and women sang laments about Josiah.
They still sing these laments today.
Israel made these laments a statute.
People wrote these laments in the Book of Laments.
passages.original: וַיְקוֹנֵ֣ן יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ עַל־ יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ כָֽל־ הַשָּׁרִ֣ים׀ וְ֠הַשָּׁרוֹת בְּקִינ֨וֹתֵיהֶ֤ם עַל־ יֹאשִׁיָּ֙הוּ֙ עַד־ הַיּ֔וֹם וַיִּתְּנ֥וּם לְחֹ֖ק עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהִנָּ֥ם כְּתוּבִ֖ים עַל־ הַקִּינֽוֹת׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Josiah, along with his deeds of loving devotion according to what is written in the Law of the LORD— his acts from beginning to end—they are indeed written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
passages.sermon:
Josiah was king of Judah.
Josiah did many acts.
Josiah showed loving devotion.
Josiah acted according to what is written in the Law of the LORD.
The rest of Josiah’s acts are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
Josiah’s first acts and last acts are written there.
passages.original: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ וַחֲסָדָ֑יו כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃ וּדְבָרָ֕יו הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־ סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִיהוּדָֽה׃
